# Relative-mesh recovery through compact intrinsic lifts

This conditional induction lemma treats vanishing coarse fiber volumes.
It has an explicit RELATIVE mesh hypothesis. It does not assert that
this hypothesis can always be achieved, and it does not prove OC.

## 1. Statement

Let k>=0, r>=1, s>=0, and m=r+s. Use coordinates
(z,u,x) in R^k times R^r times R^s. Let C_l be compact convex sets,
with all nonempty integer z-fibers indexed by one fixed finite set
P subset Z^k. All coarse fibers

    K_(l,z)={(u,x):(z,u,x) in C_l}

are assumed to lie in a fixed Euclidean ball R B_2^m, R>0. Set

    M_l=sum_(z in P) vol_m(K_(l,z))>0.

Let L_l+a_l be full-rank lattice cosets in R^r, with covolumes v_l
and measurable fundamental cells contained in [-delta_l,delta_l]^r.
Assume

    delta_l/M_l ->0.                                     (1)

No positive lower bound on M_l is imposed. The fine mixed measure is

    mu_l(A)=v_l sum_(z in P, lambda in L_l+a_l)
       vol_s({x:(z,lambda,x) in C_l intersect A}).

For s=0, vol_0 counts the singleton continuous fiber. Let S_l be the
corresponding fine mixed set and let D_l be its maximum normalized
closed ambient halfspace depth using mu_l. Its mass is positive for
all sufficiently large l, as proved below.

Put

    B(k,m)=(m+1)2^k-k-1.

Assume OC has been established for all integer ranks 0<=j<=k and all
continuous ambient dimensions at most B(k,m), including its intrinsic
lower-dimensional intersections. Then

    liminf_l D_l >= 2^(-k) Gamma_(B(k,m)).                (2)

For k=0 this assumption is only the ordinary continuous Grünbaum
theorem, because B(0,m)=m and the constructed lift has full fibers.
For s>=1 the right side of (2) is STRICTLY larger than the original
target 2^(-k-r) Gamma_s. Therefore every sufficiently late C_l satisfies
that target with a single deterministic point of S_l. The same strict
comparison holds when s=0 and r>=2. No such comparison is claimed from
(2) alone when s=0,r=1; pure integer OC is already separately proved
by Doignon.

## 2. Uniform relative discrepancy, including zero coarse-volume fibers

The sampling lemma in
`candidate 0639bd50a01557c4` gives,
for EVERY convex Q subset [-R,R]^m,

    |v_l sum_lambda vol_s(Q_lambda)-vol_m(Q)|
        <= E_l:=2r delta_l(2R+2delta_l)^(m-1).            (3)

It is proved by cell dilation/erosion and coordinate-section Fubini.
It includes lower-dimensional Q and every closed halfspace cut of Q,
without a boundary-mass exclusion.

Let nu_l be the coarse measure sum_z vol_m restricted to K_(l,z),
of total mass M_l, and write J=|P|. Then

    sup_H |mu_l(H)-nu_l(H)| <= J E_l,
    |mu_l(total)-M_l| <= J E_l.                          (4)

The total M_l is bounded above by J kappa_m R^m. Thus (1) implies
delta_l->0 and J E_l/M_l->0. In particular mu_l(total)>0 eventually.
After normalization, uniformly over ALL closed ambient halfspaces,

    |mu_l(H)/mu_l(total)-nu_l(H)/M_l|
           <= 2J E_l/(M_l-J E_l) ->0.                   (5)

This is a halfspace discrepancy statement, not total variation
convergence of the fine and coarse measures. Formula (3) is applied
also to every zero m-volume coarse fiber, so its potentially nonzero
sampled s-volume is included in (4).

## 3. Compact full-shape lift and selection of a relative interior point

Take any subsequence along which the left side of (2) is attained as a
limit, then a further subsequence such that all normalized coarse fiber
volumes converge. Set P_+={z:lim |K_(l,z)|/M_l>0}. This is nonempty
and lattice-convex. Indeed a target containing a translate of lambda
times one positive source has normalized volume at least lambda^m
times that source's positive limit. Its retained total M_(l,+) obeys

    M_(l,+)/M_l ->1.                                    (6)

After a saturated affine integer coordinate identification, P_+ has
full affine rank k'<=k. Apply
`candidate c344f12be982dcb7`
to the retained family, using total-volume normalization M_(l,+).
It gives bounded residual full m-dimensional bodies R_(l,z), positive
Hausdorff limits R_z, and compact intrinsic lifts B_l->B_* with
integer rank k', continuous ambient dimension D, and

    m<=D<=B(k',m)<=B(k,m).

All lifted fiber measures are H_m, their sum is one, and a global
affine map F_l sends them onto the retained coarse family with its
measure divided by M_(l,+). Its restriction on a component is

    x -> T_(l,i)^(-1)x + h_(l,z),
    |det T_(l,i)^(-1)|=M_(l,+).                          (7)

The maps are used only for coarse measure and halfspace comparison;
the fine lattice is still kept in the original coordinates.

By the stated lower-rank assumption, B_* has a mixed point of depth
at least 2^(-k') Gamma_D. Each of its fibers has dimension m and
positive H_m measure. Depth is continuous as the point moves inside
its own m-fiber: the lift theorem proves this by exact isolation of
components and a common-block slab estimate. Therefore for any fixed
epsilon>0 there is a point in the RELATIVE INTERIOR of some fiber z
whose lifted depth is at least

    2^(-k') Gamma_D-epsilon.                            (8)

Let x be its residual m-coordinate. Since x lies in int R_z, there
is rho>0 such that, for all sufficiently large l,

    x+rho B_2^m subset R_(l,z).                          (9)

This uses the inner inclusion of convex bodies under Hausdorff
convergence to a positive-volume limit. Total variation convergence
in each fixed lifted plane, and the lift's exact component isolation,
show that the SAME residual point has prelimit lift depth at least
(8)-o(1). Its image y_l=(z,w_l)=F_l(z,E_i x,G(z)) is in the retained
coarse source and has at least that normalized retained depth.
By (6), its depth for the full coarse measure nu_l/M_l is at least

    2^(-k') Gamma_D-epsilon-o(1).                        (10)

The center is a point in one specified original coarse fiber, not a
barycenter outside the source.

## 4. A source ball of radius proportional to M_l

Write A_l=T_(l,i)^(-1) for the selected component. By (7) and (9),

    w_l+rho A_l B_2^m subset K_(l,z) subset R B_2^m.

The difference of two points in the ellipsoid on the left has length
at most 2R. It follows that

    ||A_l|| <= R/rho.

If sigma_min(A_l) is its least singular value, the common determinant
in (7) gives

    sigma_min(A_l)
        >= M_(l,+)/(R/rho)^(m-1).

Thus the ORIGINAL fiber contains the ordinary Euclidean ball

    w_l+c M_(l,+) B_2^m subset K_(l,z),
    c=rho^m/R^(m-1)>0.                                 (11)

This is the needed quantitative interior recovery. A vanishing
coarse volume is allowed; the original inner ball shrinks at a
controlled rate. No assertion that the transformed fine lattice is
dense is needed, or made.

## 5. Fine-grid rounding and all-halfspace control

For each l the closed cubes lambda+[-delta_l,delta_l]^r cover every
base u in R^r. The fundamental cells cover almost every u, while the
union of the larger closed cubes is locally finite and closed; its
complement is open and null and therefore empty. Choose a lambda_l
whose cube contains the first r coordinates of w_l. Leave the final
s coordinates unchanged. The resulting y'_l obeys

    |y'_l-y_l|<=sqrt(r) delta_l.

By (1), (6), and (11), y'_l belongs to K_(l,z) for all large l, so
y'_l is a deterministic point of the ACTUAL fine mixed set S_l.
Ties can be settled by a fixed lexicographic rule among the finitely
many candidate lattice points in the bounded cube.

Moving a point in one coarse fiber by v changes its coarse depth
by at most

    J kappa_(m-1) R^(m-1) |v|/M_l.                      (12)

For a nonzero m-dimensional continuous part of a halfspace normal,
normalize that part to length one. Thresholds in every coarse fiber
then change by at most |v|, and Fubini bounds the lost slab by its
maximal (m-1)-section area times |v|. Pure coarse-integer normals are
unchanged. This includes arbitrary coupling between the fine integer
and continuous coordinates and all closed-boundary cuts.

Equations (1), (10), and (12) give coarse depth at y'_l at least
2^(-k') Gamma_D-epsilon-o(1). Equation (5), evaluated at this SAME
feasible point, gives the identical lower limit for fine depth.
Finally Gamma_D>=Gamma_(B(k,m)) and 2^(-k')>=2^(-k). Let epsilon
decrease to zero. Since the initial subsequence realizing the liminf
was arbitrary, (2) follows.

## 6. Constant comparison and boundary cases

For every integer a>=1, Gamma_a=(a/(a+1))^a>1/e>1/4,
and for every s>=1, Gamma_s<=1/2. Thus, when r>=1 and s>=1,

    2^(-k) Gamma_(B(k,m))
       >2^(-k)/4 >=2^(-k-r) Gamma_s.

For s=0 and r>=2, the target is 2^(-k-r), and the same strict lower
bound 2^(-k)/4 suffices. The case s=0,r=1 is excluded from this
constant-comparison corollary, with Gamma_0=1 defined explicitly.
For k=0 all lift fibers are full m-dimensional, so ordinary Grünbaum
supplies the only invoked lower-rank bound.

The fine measure differs from the usual mixed measure only by its
common positive covolume factor v_l, which cancels in normalized
depth. Eventually it has positive s-volume by (4), so its Hausdorff
dimension is s; for s=0 it is nonempty counting measure. Fibers of
zero coarse m-volume were included in the sampling estimate rather
than deleted before measuring the fine set.

The proof resolves recovery ONLY under (1). In a general normalized
sequence, delta_l/M_l need not tend to zero. Obtaining a sharp global
argument for that remaining scale regime is not supplied here.
